newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean inflation target is on track -- Aninat.
newsitem.headline: Chilean inflation target is on track -- Aninat.

text.p: New inflation figures show that Chile's annual target of 6.5 percent is likely to be met, Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat said.
Consumer prices rose a scant 0.4 percent in August and 6.4 percent over the 12 months to August, the National Statistics Institute reported. Wholesale prices also rose 0.4 percent in July, it said.

"To have a 6.4 percent annualized rate in August shows that the 6.5 percent rate for the year is perfectly viable," he said, but added that local seasonal factors may nudge up inflation in the last quarter of the year.
"We can't claim victory yet, but we think this latest one is a very good figure," he said.

Sharper monthly increases early this year, which had appeared to imperil the 6.5 percent target, were due to mainly external factors beyond the government's control, the institute's director Lenin Guardia said.

"We're satisfied that the increase in prices at the beginning of the year was influenced by external shocks, such as higher oil prices," Guardia told a news conference. Chile relies on imports for about 85 percent of its oil consumption.

Aninat said the government was concerned about unemployment, which rose again to 7.1 percent in the May-to-July quarter from 6.6 percent in April-to-June. Industrial output was also up a moderate 2.3 percent in July over July 1995, said the institute.
Both those figures gave new evidence of a sharp slowing of economic growth due to the Central Bank's tight-credit policies, known as the "ajuste," aimed at beating down inflation.
